What is the median advertised rent per s.text:
**Verified findings:**
The median advertised cold rent per square metre in Hamburg, based on 3,759 listings across four independent snapshots (Sep 2018, May 2019, Oct 2019, Feb 2020), is €13.5/m². The distribution has a mean of €14.35/m², with the 25th and 75th percentiles at €11.22/m² and €16.06/m² respectively. Median living space in these listings is 76 m² and the median number of rooms is 3.

**Interpretation:**
This median rent per square metre reflects advertised cold rents from historical snapshots and provides a broad picture of rental levels in Hamburg around the 2018-2020 period. It should not be confused with present-day market rents or official reference rents for 2025. The variation in rent per m² is considerable, indicating heterogeneous housing offers across neighborhoods and property types.

**Suggested follow-up:**
To gain deeper insight, analysis by residential location class, construction period, or property type could be informative. Also, comparison with the official Mietenspiegel 2025 might help understand shifts or gaps between advertised rents and reference rents.

Explain the Hamburg Mietenspiegel 2025..text:
Verified findings:
The Hamburg Mietenspiegel 2025 provides official reference rents (net cold rent, excluding heating and operating costs) for residential apartments in Hamburg as of April 1, 2025. It includes 88 data cells covering rent per m² by construction period of the building, residential location class ("Normale Wohnlage" or "Gute Wohnlage"), and living area category (size bands). The median reference rent across all cells is about €12.75/m². Minimum rents can be as low as €6.25/m², and maximum rents reach up to €31.65/m². The rent values are separated by categories such as construction period (e.g., up to 1918, 1919–1948, 1948–1960, and onward), quality of residential location (normal or good), and living area size bands (e.g., under 41m², 41–66m², 66–91m², etc.). The Mietenspiegel lists reference rent, minimum rent, and maximum rent per m² for each category and also reports the count of historical ImmoScout24 listings matched to those conditions and their median rents for contextual comparison.

Interpretation:
The Hamburg Mietenspiegel 2025 is a comprehensive official rent benchmark used primarily for regulatory and informational purposes to indicate typical and permissible rental levels in various segments of Hamburg’s rental housing market. It categorizes rents by building age, local residential quality, and apartment size, making it a detailed tool for estimating baseline rents based on property characteristics. It does not reflect actual current market asking rents but a regulatory reference. The matched historical listing data (n varies by category) helps see how market listings relate to these reference rents.

Suggested follow-up (if needed):
If you want, I can provide detailed reference rents for specific construction periods, locations, or apartment sizes to illustrate further how rents vary by these categories in the Mietenspiegel 2025.

What are the differences between normal.text:
Verified findings:
- The official Hamburg Mietenspiegel 2025 provides reference net cold rents per square meter (€/m²) for two residential location classes: "Normale Wohnlage" (normal residential location) and "Gute Wohnlage" (good residential location).
- For various construction periods and living-area categories, rents in good residential locations tend to be higher than in normal residential locations. For example:
  - For buildings constructed by 31.12.1918 with living area under 41m², the reference rent is about 13.77 €/m² in a normal location vs. 13.02 €/m² in a good location, but the maximum and median rents from listings tend to be higher in good locations.
  - For buildings constructed 1968-1977, median reference rents in good locations generally range from about 6.6 to 31.65 €/m², higher than normal locations' range which has some lower limits around 6.25 €/m² and maximums around 25 €/m².
- The Mietenspiegel shows differentiated rent scales by both residential location and living-area category, indicating these characteristics are key factors in rent estimation.
- Sample sizes for historical listings vary and can be small in some categories (often below 10 listings), so median listing rents should be interpreted cautiously.

Interpretation:
- Good residential location is associated with generally higher reference rents and higher maximum rent ceilings compared to normal residential location in Hamburg, reflecting the perceived attractiveness or demand for these areas.
- The rent differences vary by building age and size segments, showing that location quality is one important dimension among others.
- Small sample sizes in some categories reduce reliability of listing-based median rent comparisons.

Suggested follow-up (if needed):
- Analyze rent differences by construction period and size more closely for a quantitative summary.
- Compare rent distributions spatially using neighbourhood-level data to refine understanding of location class effects.

Prepare an executive summary of the avai.text:
Verified findings: 
The available data includes 3,759 Hamburg rental listings from four independent ImmoScout24 snapshots between Sep 2018 and Feb 2020 across 94 neighbourhoods. Median rent per m² is 13.5 €/m², with a mean of 14.35 €/m². The interquartile range is from 11.22 €/m² (25th percentile) to 16.07 €/m² (75th percentile), with minimum and maximum rents at 4.35 €/m² and 61.25 €/m² respectively. Median living space is 76 m², median rooms count is 3, and median base cold rent is 1,014 EUR. No filters were applied.

Interpretation:
The rent distribution shows a wide range with some higher outliers. The median rent per m² around 13.5 €/m² is a central tendency across various neighbourhoods and types. The typical listing targets around 3-room apartments with moderate living space. These figures represent historic advertised cold rents and should not be considered current or legal rent values.

Suggested follow-up:
A breakdown by key factors such as construction period, equipment level, and neighbourhood class would provide further insights. Comparing these listings to the official Hamburg Mietenspiegel 2025 benchmarks might clarify rental levels relative to regulatory references.

Verified findings:
The top 10 neighbourhoods by number of listings (n≥84) in Hamburg are:
- Rahlstedt (187 listings), median rent per m² 11.41 €
- Winterhude (139 listings), median 17.00 €
- Bergedorf (133 listings), median 12.10 €
- Langenhorn (126 listings), median 13.08 €
- Harburg (97 listings), median 12.68 €
- HafenCity (89 listings), median 20.29 €
- Wellingsbüttel (87 listings), median 13.75 €
- Bramfeld (85 listings), median 12.55 €
- Poppenbüttel (84 listings), median 12.98 €
- Wandsbek (84 listings), median 12.02 €

All neighbourhood samples have at least 84 listings and stable data coverage with no filters applied.

Interpretation:
Neighbourhoods with both high listing counts and a broad range of median rents like Winterhude and HafenCity stand out due to upper median rents (17.00 €/m² and 20.29 €/m² respectively). Rahlstedt has the largest sample but a lower median rent (11.41 €/m²). Investigation into price dispersion, outliers, and trends in these areas may be informative. Lower priced neighbourhoods with large samples like Bergedorf and Bramfeld can also be benchmarked.

Suggested follow-up:
Further investigation could focus on:
- Rent trends over time for these neighbourhoods
- Distribution and outliers in rents within them
- Comparisons with official Mietenspiegel 2025 benchmarks by location and property type
- Specific characteristics driving rent variation (size, age, amenities)

This would help understand differences in rental dynamics across diverse neighbourhoods with good data coverage.

What factors appear associated with high.text:
**Verified findings:**

- Room count: 1-room listings have the highest median rent per m² at 15.03€/m² (n=337), with rents generally decreasing for 1.5–4 rooms, then slightly increasing again beyond 4.5 rooms.
- Size: Very small apartments (<40 m²) have the highest median rent per m² at 16.74€/m² (n=264). For bigger sizes, median rents tend to be around 12.64–14.44€/m².
- Construction year: Oldest buildings (before 1919) have a median rent of 15.00€/m² (n=396), newer buildings around 2016–2020 have median 14.76€/m² (n=894), with other periods generally lower.
- Property type: Penthouse (median 15.5€/m², n=113) and half-basement units (15.79€/m², n=23) stand out with higher rents. Apartments have median 13.68€/m² (n=2090).
- Features: Listings with a lift have median rent 14.50€/m² (n=1486) vs. 12.63€/m² without (n=2273). New constructions median is 14.68€/m² (n=633) vs. 13.11€/m² older listings (n=3126).
- Balcony and garden presence show slight median rent differences: balcony yes 13.5€/m² versus no 13.42€/m²; garden yes 13.73€/m² versus no 13.45€/m² (n>600 each).

**Interpretation:**

Higher advertised rents per m² tend to be associated with smaller apartment sizes, fewer rooms (especially 1-room), early or very recent construction years, penthouse or special property types, presence of a lift, and new construction status. Features like balconies and gardens show only mild associations with rent per m².

**Suggested follow-up:**

A multivariate analysis accounting for interaction effects between these factors (location, size, age, features) could provide better understanding of combined influences on advertised rents. Also comparing with Mietenspiegel 2025 reference rents by these factors could help interpret relative positions.

Show the Mietenspiegel range for a Gute.text:
Verified findings: 
For Gute Wohnlage residential location and buildings constructed from 1994 to 2010, the Hamburg Mietenspiegel 2025 gives the following net cold rent per m² ranges by living area category:
- Up to 41 m²: €12.02 to €17.11, reference €14.19 (n=3 listings)
- 41 to under 66 m²: €10.72 to €15.76, reference €13.78 (n=8)
- 66 to under 91 m²: €10.03 to €16.29, reference €13.18 (n=15)
- 91 to under 131 m²: €11.59 to €19.00, reference €14.63 (n=29)
- 131 m² and above: €12.06 to €19.31, reference €16.00 (n=23)

Interpretation:
The reference rent (official mean) tends to be slightly lower for medium-sized apartments around 66-91 m², with larger apartments above 131 m² showing the highest reference rent. The ranges reflect legal minimum and maximum bandwidths for cold rents excluding heating and operating costs. Sample sizes vary, with some smaller categories (e.g., <41 m²) having low listing counts (n=3), which advises cautious interpretation.

If you want, I can provide corresponding historical listing rents for comparison or focus on a specific living area category or neighborhood within Gute Wohnlage.
